svg.text: M1 blueprint with the video path
Solid = recommended and committed · dashed = optional, deferred, or rejected
Baked in — no upload, no volume
its own early layer → cached on later pushes
single-platform image · clip rides inside it
CARSKY ROOM — runtime (R5 deployment · R6 network)
read-only image layer — the file is already there at start
R3 track store · R13 gate · R14 risk · R15 emit
AAOS guest · team APK installed over ADB
R16 layout · R17 God view of ego, B, ghost C
plays the SAME clip — over TCP 8080 from a static
server on the ADA node, or from a local APK copy.
OPTIONAL — no M1 requirement covers it
one ethernet pin per node, wired like-to-like · all inter-ECU traffic is UDP over this L2 network · no VIDEO pin is declared
the node pulls the image at deploy — clip included
REJECTED — fanning a live feed out over CarSky's video pin
Container ↔ Container: the video pin is an iceoryx2 shared-memory transport carrying raw RGBA — ≈ 70 MB/s at 720p20, with no C++ helper and an undocumented frame header.
Container → Skycraft: the guest side of a video pin is one sentence in the platform doc — no wiring example, no named counterpart, no camera HAL. Unusable inside the deadline.
LEGEND — every R-number is a requirement ID from the report §2. There is no separate "message" numbering.

R1–R6 are the CONTRACT requirements: each one's deliverable is a schema or a topology — which is why "the R2 message" or "an R3 object" reads like a message name. It is shorthand for the artifact that requirement defines. R7–R19 are BEHAVIOURAL requirements: the deliverable is running code.
ETSI CPM profile (ASN.1 UPER) — the over-the-air message
V2X ECU → ADA object message (JSON over UDP)
TrackedObject schema — one shape for every ego object
ADA → IVI warning + state message (JSON over UDP)
node deployment — one ECU = one node of one blueprint
Ethernet Bridge + one ethernet pin per node
object detection from video (YOLO11n ONNX, CPU)
track store + admission gate (30 m, hysteresis)
Collision Risk Assessment abstraction + NLOS plugin
warning output — what emits an R4 message
HMI layout on the AAOS node
warning view — God view of ego, B and ghost C

ego = vehicle A, the warned car, always the frame origin (0, 0) · B = the visible occluder ahead, the only vehicle A's own camera should ever detect · C = the occluded car, known to A only through the relay.
